title: Hazardous Waste on the Jobsite
basis: EPA's Categories of Hazardous Waste Generators page, with 29 CFR 1926.25(c) and 1926.252(e)
summary: Waste that is hazardous cannot go in the regular dumpster. The company that generates it has legal duties for identifying it, how much it can keep and who takes it away.
talking_points: Containers for garbage and for oily, flammable or hazardous waste, such as caustics, acids and harmful dusts, must have covers, and waste must be disposed of at frequent and regular intervals (29 CFR 1926.25(c)).
Keep solvent waste, oily rags and flammable liquids in fire-resistant covered containers until they are removed from the site (1926.252(e)).
EPA says a generator must identify all the hazardous waste it produces. The monthly amount sets which rules apply.

Very small quantity generator: 100 kilograms or less of hazardous waste a month, or 1 kilogram or less of acutely hazardous waste. It may not accumulate more than 1,000 kilograms at any time and must deliver the waste to a person or facility authorized to manage it.

Small quantity generator: more than 100 but less than 1,000 kilograms a month. It may keep waste on site up to 180 days without a permit (270 days if shipping more than 200 miles), and never more than 6,000 kilograms.
Large quantity generator: 1,000 kilograms or more a month, or more than 1 kilogram of acutely hazardous waste. It may keep waste on site for no more than 90 days.
Good practice: do not mix hazardous waste with ordinary trash, keep containers closed, and ask your supervisor who manages hazardous waste on this job before you dispose of anything.
Good practice: ask your company's environmental contact which generator category this job falls in and what your state also requires.
site_hazards_to_check: Solvent, paint or oily rag waste in an open or general trash container
Hazardous waste piling up with no pickup arranged
Waste containers near a drain or ignition source
No one named to manage hazardous waste on the job
discussion_questions: What hazardous waste do we produce on this job, and where does it go?
Who signs off on hazardous waste pickup here?
What should you do with leftover paint, solvent or oily rags at the end of the shift?
